claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 6 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's great to know you're looking to claim for Alex, who is 6 years old.

Now, could you please tell me if you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that.

Do you live with Alex, or if not, do you contribute at least the same amount as Child Benefit (currently £25.60 per week for the eldest child) towards looking after him, for example on food, clothes, or pocket money?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me, and I'm not currently contributing financially towards his care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know.

Since Alex doesn't live with you and you're not currently contributing financially towards his care, I need to ask a couple more questions to understand your situation fully.

Has Alex recently moved to live with someone else (within the last 8 weeks), or has he been living elsewhere for longer than that?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been living elsewhere for longer than that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

Based on what you've told me, I need to ask one more question: Is someone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure if someone else is claiming it or not.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know.

Based on the information you've provided, I now have enough to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you would not currently be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

To qualify for Child Benefit, you normally need to be considered 'responsible' for the child. This means you must either:
1. **Live with the child**, or
2. **Contribute at least the same amount as Child Benefit** (currently £25.60 per week for an eldest or only child) towards looking after them — for example, on food, clothes, or pocket money.

In your situation:
- Alex doesn't live with you
- You're not currently contributing financially towards his care
- He has been living elsewhere for more than 8 weeks

When a child goes to live with someone else, you can usually continue to receive Child Benefit for up to 8 weeks, but since Alex has been living elsewhere longer than that and you're not contributing to his upkeep, you wouldn't qualify.

**What you could do:**
- If you start contributing to Alex's upkeep at an amount equal to or greater than the Child Benefit rate, you may become eligible. You could contact the Child Benefit Office to discuss this.
- If the person Alex is living with isn't already claiming Child Benefit for him, they may be able to claim instead.

I hope this information is helpful. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
